newsitem.title: USA: US, EU trade chiefs optimistic on dispute solution.
newsitem.headline: US, EU trade chiefs optimistic on dispute solution.

text.p: U.S. and European Union trade officials said Friday they were optimistic that a dispute over an agreement to eliminate tariffs on a wide range of information technologies could be resolved.
EU spokesman Peter Guilford said "there is a fair chance" the issue could be resolved during the two-day meeting of the trade ministers from Japan, Canada, the European Union and the United States.

The Quadrilateral (Quad) trade chiefs hope they can settle their differences over the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) so that the international accord can be launched at the first meeting of World Trade Organization ministers in December in Singapore.

"We want to help to make sure that what happens in Singapore is going to be forward looking and that it will be a successful conference," Canadian Trade Minister Arthur Eggleton told reporters ahead of a morning session.
U.S. trade officials have said there would be little chance of the ITA being agreed to at the December WTO meeting if Quad members were unable to agree among themselves.

The ITA would eliminate tariffs by 2000 on a wide range of electronic products, including computers, chips, software, fax machines, modems and other telecommunications equipment. U.S. Trade Representative spokesman Jay Ziegler said that the idea of eliminating tariffs on those products is not negotiable.
European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan has said the main stumbling block is the U.S./Japan semiconductor alliance.
EU officials have said they are concerned that European firms would be discriminated against if the wider ITA failed to get off the ground.

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky has said the semiconductor issue could easily be resolved and suggested the real obstacle was a lack of unity among European Union members. Barshefsky and Brittan met late Thursday to discuss the ITA and experts from both sides have continued working on proposals in an effort to reach agreement, officials said.

The four trade ministers were discuss a number of issues concerning the upcoming WTO meeting. The issues include telecommunications and efforts to reach a global market opening agreement by mid-February, officials said.
